clue.text: Fellow player leaves pitch

parts.note: cos is a lettuce, here standing for its leaves
pitch is the black sticky substance tar

explanation.surface: A footballer walks off the field mid-match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb (departs) but is the noun: cos lettuce leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-star is an actor sharing top billing, so a fellow performer in the same production.

clue.text: Manage to negotiate bend in car

indicators.note: to negotiate a bend is to go round it, so the word for manage wraps round the bend's letter

parts.note: to manage is to cope
a U-bend, so U stands for a bend

explanation.surface: A driver gets round a corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupé is a two-door car with a fixed roof, a specific kind of motor.

clue.text: Agitate around radius bone

indicators.note: around tells us the phrase for agitate goes round the letter for radius

parts.note: to agitate is to stir up

explanation.surface: Fiddling with the forearm bone called the radius.
explanation.walkthrough: The radius is a real arm bone, which makes 'radius bone' look like one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The stirrup, or stapes, is the tiny bone in the middle ear.

clue.text: Throbbing uvulas? Not half! Carnal relations can be so described

indicators.note: throbbing suggests pulsing movement, so the letters are shaken into a new order
not half means only the first half of the word uvulas is kept

explanation.surface: A lurid remark about throbbing throats and carnal relations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' poses as an exclamation, but keeps UVU from UVULAS; 'Throbbing' shuffles UVU with CARNAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Avuncular means like an uncle, and uncles are relations, so uncles may be described with this adjective.

clue.text: Nullify threat from doctor as I'm about to perform an amputation?

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are moved round into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A surgeon announces an imminent amputation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to perform an amputation?' adds a second, punning reading: dis-arm is to remove an arm.
explanation.definitionFit: To disarm someone is to take away their weapons, so nullifying the danger they pose.

clue.text: White Welshman last seen in Caerphilly

parts.note: Ivor is a typically Welsh man's name

indicators.note: last seen in points to the final letter of the word Caerphilly

explanation.surface: A white-skinned Welshman was last spotted in the town of Caerphilly.
explanation.walkthrough: Caerphilly is a Welsh town and also a white crumbly cheese, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivory is a creamy off-white colour, from elephant tusks.

clue.text: Partly reveal a story regarding Shelley's youth

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Give away part of a tale about the young poet Shelley.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelley's poem 'Alastor, or the Spirit of Solitude' tells of a young poet, so the title is regarding a youth.

clue.text: Person looking after online discussion upset Romeo? Drat!

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of the following words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A forum admin annoys a would-be lover, who curses.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum moderator polices a web discussion, keeping posts within the rules.

clue.text: Obedient daughter — lovely, but no princess in short

indicators.note: but no says the princess's name is taken away from the word for lovely

parts.note: lovely means beautiful
Princess Beatrice is shortened to Bea

explanation.surface: A well-behaved daughter is pretty, but not royal.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Beatrice, a granddaughter of Elizabeth II, is known as Bea.
explanation.definitionFit: Dutiful means doing what duty requires, hence compliant and well behaved.

clue.text: In direction of pull, a road south

parts.note: to tow is to pull behind
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Directions: a pull along a road heading south.
explanation.definitionFit: Towards is a preposition meaning moving in the direction of something.

clue.text: Doctor Who crashed into tree, light being made of it?

definitions.text: tree, light being made of it?

indicators.note: something crashed is smashed up, so the letters are wrecked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The Doctor's time machine has crashed into a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Torchwood is also a Doctor Who spin-off series, a neat link to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Torchwood is a resinous tree whose wood burns well, so torches giving light are made of it.

clue.text: Unruly youngster starts on telescope?

parts.note: a refractor is a telescope that uses lenses

indicators.note: starts points to the opening letter of the word youngster

explanation.surface: A wild child begins using a telescope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets the opening letter after the telescope word in this across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Refractory means stubborn and hard to control, so disobedient.

clue.text: Necklace of gold kept by the Celts, primarily

indicators.note: kept by says the gold is held inside the other letters
primarily points to the first letters of the words the and Celts

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A gold necklace was treasured by ancient Celtic people.
explanation.definitionFit: A torc is a rigid twisted neck ring, worn by Celtic peoples, so a kind of necklace.

clue.text: Stupid lapse, bit of a bloomer

indicators.note: stupid suggests something muddled, so the letters of lapse are jumbled

explanation.surface: A daft lapse is a bit of a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a mistake, but here is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A sepal is one of the leaf-like parts round a flower, so part of a bloom.

clue.text: A revolutionary's supporting PR section of the Greens

indicators.note: supporting in a down answer means placed underneath, so this part comes below

parts.note: public relations is spin
Che Guevara is the crossword's standard revolutionary, with the possessive giving S

explanation.surface: A rebel backs a publicity wing of the Green Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Greens' suggests the political party; it means leafy vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy vegetable, and the plural forms one group among greens.

clue.text: Singers missing parts thrown away by tenor in a state

parts.note: to cast is to throw away

indicators.note: in says A and the tenor's letter sit inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: RI is Rhode Island, a US state
T is the abbreviation for tenor in music

explanation.surface: Choristers lose their parts, which a tenor tosses aside in a fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Castrati were male singers castrated before puberty, so literally lacking body parts.

clue.text: Bare bum finally administered with heartless slap outside seed store

indicators.note: outside says the slap word wraps round the rest
heartless means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: to spank is to slap

indicators.note: administered suggests the letters are dealt out in a new order
finally points to the last letter of the word bum

explanation.surface: A naughty scene: a smack on a bare bottom, in a seed shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the middle of the slap word; 'administered' jumbles the bare letters with the bum's last, and 'outside' wraps the slap round them.
explanation.definitionFit: A sperm bank is a facility that keeps donated sperm, the human seed, in storage.

clue.text: Cancel comic taking off 'hard women'

parts.note: a wit is a comic, someone who is funny

indicators.note: taking off means mimicking, so the word hard is played around with

explanation.surface: A comedian doing an impression of tough women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking off' reads as removing, but means parodying: HARD is jumbled to HDRA.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw an offer or order is to cancel it, taking it back.

clue.text: Melancholy? Not me — 50, newly happy and carefree

indicators.note: newly signals the remaining letters are made anew in a different order
not says the following letters are taken away from the word melancholy

parts.note: taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A fifty-year-old says gloom is behind them: they are newly cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' takes ME and L from MELANCHOLY, leaving ANCHOY, which 'newly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Halcyon days are idyllic, peaceful and happy times.

clue.text: Glower as month ends

indicators.note: ends means only the tail end of the month's name is kept, cutting its start

parts.note: November is a month

explanation.surface: Someone scowls as the month draws to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: September, November and December all end this way. 'Glower' looks like scowl, but is a thing that glows.
explanation.definitionFit: An ember is a smouldering piece of coal or wood, something that glows.

clue.text: Mexican food — donkey eats it

indicators.note: eats means the donkey word takes the other inside it

parts.note: a burro is a small donkey

explanation.surface: A donkey snacks on a Mexican dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrito is a Mexican tortilla wrap filled with beans or meat.

clue.text: Computer left in college dining room

parts.note: HAL is the computer in the film 2001: A Space Odyssey

explanation.surface: A laptop was left behind in the college refectory.
explanation.definitionFit: At British universities the hall is the large room where college members eat.

clue.text: Start to make for port, so potentially protected from bad weather

indicators.note: potentially says these letters could become something else when rearranged
start to points to the opening letter of the word make

explanation.surface: A sailor heads for harbour to shelter from a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormproof describes something built to withstand storms, so shielded from rough weather.

clue.text: Keep mum working at a foreign language

parts.note: keeping mum is keeping quiet, which sh demands
on means working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A mother keeps quiet while learning another language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like mother, but 'keep mum' means stay silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Shona is a Bantu language spoken mainly in Zimbabwe.

clue.text: A little bird told me: new wife needed for Dutch male

indicators.note: new signals that the resulting letters are freshly arranged
needed for says one letter goes in place of others

explanation.surface: Gossip: the Dutchman needs a new wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little bird told me' looks like an idiom, but splits: W replaces D and M in TOLDME, and 'new' rearranges TOLWE.
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is a young or small owl, literally a little bird.

clue.text: Crikey! In short, that's some tomgirl

parts.note: some of the letters of tomgirl spell the texting abbreviation OMG, which is the short form of the exclamation

explanation.surface: Wow: what a tomboy!
explanation.walkthrough: The letters OMG sit inside 'tomgirl', and 'In short' says they abbreviate the full phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise or shock.

clue.text: Recipe, first from Italy involving one oval cooking dish

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, as on prescriptions

indicators.note: cooking suggests things being prepared or altered, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: first from points to the opening letter of the word Italy

explanation.surface: An Italian recipe for an oval baking dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dish' looks like the oval cooking vessel, but means the food.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are filled pasta parcels, a classic Italian food.

clue.text: Footwear available in Boots and Aldi

indicators.note: available in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Shoes on sale at a chemist and a discount supermarket.
explanation.walkthrough: Boots is a British high-street chemist chain and Aldi a discount supermarket; 'Boots' also suggests footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandal is an open shoe held on by straps, a kind of footwear.

clue.text: Make last electronic transfer to UK when touring Spain

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the rearranged letters surround the letter for Spain
transfer means moved about, so the letters of to UK are rearranged

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A bank transfer to Britain while on holiday in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: To eke out supplies is to make them stretch further, using them sparingly.
